title: VentAssist vs IntelliLung — comparison table

scope.arena: their reward, ported faithfully (benchmark/rewards_intellilung.py), trained and scored inside the VentAssist MDP
scope.not_the_arena: their 26-dim state / their split / their frozen DistFQE (Phase 2) — blocked: they ship no weights and no data, and their MIMIC pipeline needs a populated Postgres `mimic` DB

battery_honest_negatives.note: The single-seed Layer 2 result reported 8/8 for our reward. Across 5 seeds it is 6.6/8 [5.920022, 7.279978]. The 8/8 was a lucky seed and must not be quoted. Report the per-case rates.

table_b_agreement_trap.rule: Never report clinician agreement without a value estimate and an action-diversity figure beside it.
table_b_agreement_trap.why: Clinicians hold 77.65 % of the time, so any policy that holds more scores better on agreement. Agreement improves as the policy gets worse.
table_b_agreement_trap.generalises: IntelliLung's own Rule 5, extended from likelihood to agreement

observations.case: IPW on vs off (5 seeds each, matched budget)

observations.but: it rose because the policy's own preferred action (cut TV) had been suppressed; confidence is computed over allowed actions only, so removing 100 competitors makes a forced hold look sharper (SUMMARY §15.11 B2)

table_c_ventassist_vs_clinician.rule5_partial: Item 7 of Phase 1 is PARTIAL by design. The clinician action log-likelihood is a property of the behaviour policy, not of our training seeds, so it is identical across seeds and is computed once in action_density.py. The triple is therefore assembled from two artifacts, not one. Stated here so a reviewer does not find it unaided.

action_likelihood_rule5_gate.reading: Delta > 0 means the policy's actions are ON-SUPPORT under the clinician density model — not extrapolation. The sign is what Rule 5 asks for; the margin is small.

safety_violations.reading: The policy violates less often on every rule measured.

caveat.driving_pressure_gt_15: requires airway-pressure waveform (not available) — not imputed

checkpoint_selection.question: Does the checkpoint_every=500 fix produce a model that should replace the deployed one?
checkpoint_selection.finding: Validation Q-loss and FQE disagree about which checkpoint is best, and the finer interval moved selection AWAY from the FQE optimum. Q-loss improves reproducibly and with non-overlapping CIs (1.5340 -> 1.4802), but FQE does not follow: 2.4823 -> 2.0016, and the interval widens 0.1010 -> 0.6423. By selected step the value estimate is NON-MONOTONIC and peaks near 10,000: ~5,750 -> 2.0016, ~10,000 -> 2.4823, ~27,000 (deployed) -> 1.8787.
checkpoint_selection.consequence_for_the_retrain_claim: The deployed checkpoint sits 0.50 BELOW the coarse arm's lower bound, which is the basis of the SUMMARY §15.11 C6 claim that it underperforms a retrain by more than seed noise. Against the arm trained with the FIXED config it sits INSIDE the interval. So that claim holds only against the coarse arm, and the case for replacing the deployed artifact is NOT made. Do not deploy on this evidence.
checkpoint_selection.third_criterion: A THIRD criterion disagrees with both, and it is the one the deploy gate enforces: the 8-case clinical battery improves monotonically with selected step — 6.60/8 at ~5,750, 7.20/8 at ~10,000, 8.00/8 for the deployed ~27,000 model. `high_peep` ('PEEP is 18, lower it') is a safety reflex acquired LATE: 0 of 5 seeds have it at ~5,750, 2 of 5 at ~10,000, and the deployed model has it. Selecting on validation Q-loss therefore selects a model that has not yet learned a clinical safety reflex the deployed one has. Evidence: benchmark/checkpoint_battery.py.
checkpoint_selection.what_does_hold: Two things improve in the fine arm and are worth keeping: validation Q-loss (separated CIs) and the safety violation rate (0.3375 -> 0.3128, also separated). The lung-protective dTV bias excludes zero in BOTH arms, so it does not depend on the selection rule.

model_free_leads.note: These two do not depend on our reward or our learned dynamics, so they are the results to lead with.

model_based_rollout_safety.warning: MODEL-BASED. These come from NWE rollouts under our LEARNED dynamics over T=12 steps from n_starts=400, and the hypoxaemia row rests on only 44 episodes. They are far weaker evidence than the 198,050-transition model-free numbers in C3/C4 and must never be quoted beside them without this distinction.

confidence.quote_which: monotonicity (Spearman), not ECE — the achievable range is [0.3, 0.8491], so a near-zero ECE is structurally impossible

table_d_capabilities.claim: Reward carries a direct action signal
table_d_capabilities.intellilung: NO — the action is absent from their entire reward INTERFACE
table_d_capabilities.source: algo_src/reward/base.py:7 — the abstract signature is `__call__(self, dataset, terminated, pre_process_configs, **kwargs)`, with no action parameter. All five implementations inherit it (range.py, ventilator_free_days.py x2, mortality.py, stacking.py) and `grep -n action algo_src/reward/*.py` returns NOTHING. So this is not a property of the reward they happened to choose — their abstraction cannot express an action-dependent reward at all.

table_d_capabilities.claim: The WHOLE composite reward is action-independent, not just RangeReward
table_d_capabilities.intellilung: yes — both components are functions of state/outcome columns
table_d_capabilities.source: Their configured reward is AddRewards([RangeReward, VFDEachStep]) (algo_src/configs/pre_processing_configs.yaml). RangeReward reads next_states only; VFDEachStep reads pause_until_next, mv_duration and daemo_discharge (algo_src/reward/ventilator_free_days.py:57) — all dataset state/outcome columns. MortalityReward likewise reads daemo_discharge only. This closes the obvious objection that our port covers only half their reward and the other half might carry the action signal: it does not.

table_d_capabilities.claim: Current ventilator settings present in the state (makes delta-actions well-posed)
table_d_capabilities.ventassist: yes — PEEP, TV and FiO2 are all state features
table_d_capabilities.intellilung: partially — PEEP and FiO2 are NOT in the state, only actions
table_d_capabilities.source: algo_src/configs/pre_processing_configs.yaml: both experiment blocks have exactly 26 state_vector_columns, which include `vent_pinsp` and `vent_vt_obs` but NOT `vent_peep` or `vent_fio2` — those two appear only under action_space. REFINEMENT to BENCHMARK_PLAN §0 trap 3, which says their state lacks 'the current PEEP/FiO2 settings': correct for PEEP and FiO2, but their state DOES carry observed tidal volume, so the claim must not be widened to all three knobs.

table_d_capabilities.claim: Mode-aware action masking enabled by default
table_d_capabilities.source: algo_src/dataset/pre_processing_configs.py:28 `vent_mode_action_masking: bool = False`; both shipped config blocks (algo_src/configs/pre_processing_configs.yaml:96,191) set it false

table_d_capabilities.claim: Safety-violation rates measured against the clinician
table_d_capabilities.ventassist: yes — 5 rules, policy lower on every one
table_d_capabilities.intellilung: no such metric in the repository
table_d_capabilities.source: BENCHMARK_HANDOFF.md (their Rule 9); no violation-rate metric found in algo_src/

table_d_capabilities.claim: Enforced safety filter + hard deploy gate
Decision resolution finer than theirs (1 h vs 4 h)
table_d_capabilities.source: RETRACTED. data_pipelines/MIMIC/.env.example:8 `RESOLUTION = 3600` is the decision timestep (consumed by create_time_windows(..., resolution), time_window_creation.py:170,247); their own comment at line 292 reads 'during the 1h resolution time'. The 4 h in their code is the drug/fluid LOOK-BACK window (drugs_vaso4h, state_ivfluid4h), not the timestep. BENCHMARK_PLAN differentiator #4 and the §1 'their 4h for the head-to-head' decision are both wrong and must be struck.

claim_boundaries: The defensible claim is NO WORSE THAN THE CLINICIAN — never 'better than doctors'.
Every value number is computed under VentAssist's own reward and its own learned dynamics. FQE values are not comparable across different rewards.
Retrospective, single cohort, unmeasured confounding, no prospective validation.
Waveform influence is EXACTLY 0.0 — Track B's checkpoint is Track A's weights with an untouched [I | 0] adapter (selected_step = 0). An honest negative result on 35 patients / 895 transitions.
Responsiveness > 0 is entirely unvalidated; every number here is at responsiveness 0.
IPW addresses MEASURED confounding only, and as implemented it makes the policy worse.
Table A is their REWARD in OUR arena. It is not a comparison against their published model, which was trained on MIMIC + eICU + HiRID and whose weights they do not ship.
Their 'Hybrid-IQL' means a hybrid ACTION SPACE; our 'HybridIQL' is discrete IQL + CQL + a feature adapter. Rename ours before publication to avoid the collision.
